threads.thread_goal: Align on candidate dishes and lock the final seasonal lunch menu list.

messages.text: Team, I've put together a draft of candidate seasonal dishes in A1. We have 8 options covering meat, fish, vegetarian, and vegan categories. Each one is tagged so we can see what we're working with. Please review and let me know which ones you think will work best for our kitchen setup and timeline. We need to lock this down so we can move into full recipe development.

Good start. I'm looking at the vegetarian options—we have two listed. Given the demand we see, I think we should aim for at least three vegetarian and one vegan option on the final menu. That gives us flexibility and covers dietary preferences.

I agree with that split. Looking at the fish options, the pan-seared sea bass and the baked cod both fit our prep capacity. The bass is more interesting but requires a bit more finesse. The cod is solid and reliable. What's the thinking on complexity here—do we want to push ourselves or keep it straightforward?

The sea bass is doable if we batch the prep correctly. I'd lean toward including it because it's seasonal and it gives us a premium option. The cod stays as backup. For the meat dishes, I'm confident about the herb-crusted chicken and the braised beef. Both work with our current equipment and timing.

Quick question—on the vegetarian side, are we including the roasted vegetable tart and the lentil risotto? Both are on the list but I want to make sure we're not overloading ourselves with too many components.

The tart requires pastry work which we can prep ahead. The risotto is more hands-on during service. If we're tight on time, I'd suggest the tart plus one simpler vegetarian option—maybe the roasted vegetable plate with grain. That keeps variety without stretching us too thin.
I can handle the pastry prep for the tart. Just need clear instructions on timing and storage. What about the vegan option—I see we have a chickpea curry listed. Is that the direction we want to go?

The chickpea curry works well. It's flavorful, holds well, and fits our spice profile. I'd go with that as our vegan anchor. So if we're settling on: herb-crusted chicken, braised beef, sea bass, roasted vegetable tart, roasted vegetable plate with grain, chickpea curry, and maybe one more vegetarian option—that's seven dishes. Do we want an eighth or are we good with seven?

Seven is solid. That gives us two meat, one fish, three vegetarian, and one vegan. Covers the range and keeps prep manageable. Let me confirm: we're locking in herb-crusted chicken, braised beef, pan-seared sea bass, roasted vegetable tart, roasted vegetable plate with grain, chickpea curry, and the baked cod as a backup option. Does that work for everyone?
Confirmed. That's a solid lineup. The backup cod gives us flexibility if the sea bass has any supply issues. Ready to move into recipe development with these seven.
Good. I'll start pulling together the detailed recipes for the vegetable dishes. Should have those ready by tomorrow.
I'll work on the tart recipe and pastry timing. Want to make sure the dough prep doesn't conflict with other morning tasks.

Perfect. I'll handle the chicken, beef, and sea bass recipes. We'll consolidate everything into A2 by end of week. Once we have the full recipes, we can start costing them out against our target food cost.
I'll coordinate the chickpea curry recipe and make sure we have the spice sourcing locked down. Also want to double-check our supplier options for consistency.

Great. So we have the menu locked. Next step is full recipes and costing. Let's aim to have all recipes drafted by Friday so we can review and cost them out next week. That keeps us on track for the 21-day timeline.

threads.thread_goal: Define recipes, portions, and costing for each approved dish.

messages.text: Recipes are in. I've compiled the first draft of A2 with all seven dishes—ingredients, steps, and portion sizes. I've also started the costing sheet in A3 using current supplier prices. A few dishes are coming in above our target food cost percentage, so we need to review and decide on adjustments. Let me know what you see.

I've reviewed the costing. The sea bass is running about 3% over target because of the current market price. The herb-crusted chicken is solid. The braised beef is also slightly high. For the sea bass, we have a couple of options: reduce the portion by 20 grams, or source from a different supplier. I checked with our secondary supplier and they're about 8% cheaper. What's the preference?

The secondary supplier is reliable. I've worked with them before. The quality is consistent. I'd go with the supplier switch rather than reducing portion—the 180-gram portion is already lean for a fish main. That keeps the dish premium without cutting into the plate.

Agreed. I'll update the costing to reflect the secondary supplier for sea bass. That brings us within target. Now the braised beef—it's running about 2% over. The issue is the cut we're using. We could either reduce the portion slightly or switch to a leaner cut that braises just as well. The chuck is what I specified, but we could use brisket point instead.
The brisket point will work. It's actually more forgiving in the braise—longer cook time but more consistent texture. I'd go that route. What about the vegetable dishes? Are those tracking okay?

The tart is good. The pastry and filling are within budget. The roasted vegetable plate is solid too. The chickpea curry—I want to check the spice costs. Some of those spices can vary. Should we verify the costing on that one?

Good catch. I've already sourced the spices. The costing in A3 reflects bulk pricing from our main supplier. We're within target on the curry. The portion is 280 grams, which is generous for a vegetarian main and keeps the cost reasonable.

So we're adjusting: sea bass supplier switch, braised beef to brisket point. Those two changes bring everything within target. Let me update A3 and A2 with the revised recipes. The portions are: chicken 200g, beef 220g, sea bass 180g, tart 240g, vegetable plate 300g, curry 280g. Does that lock in for everyone?
Confirmed. Those portions are solid and the costing is clean. The ingredient substitutions make sense—brisket point is actually a better choice for the braise. Ready to move into prep planning.
Agreed. Once we have the final recipes locked, I can start mapping out the prep schedule. Need to know which dishes require overnight prep and which can be done morning-of.

I'll have the updated A2 and A3 finalized by EOD today. The beef braise and the tart dough both need overnight. The sea bass and chicken can be prepped morning-of. Vegetables for the plate can be prepped the day before and stored properly. We'll detail all that in the prep schedule next.

threads.thread_goal: Set up prep workflow, food safety checklist, and allergen reference.

messages.text: I've mapped out the daily prep schedule based on our final recipes. The plan separates cold and hot prep, assigns responsibilities, and accounts for our current staffing and opening hours. I've also drafted A4 with the food safety checklist and A6 with allergen and dietary flags for all seven dishes. Both are ready for review.

Good work. I'm looking at the prep schedule. The overnight items are the beef braise and tart dough—both start at 6 AM. Morning prep for sea bass and chicken starts at 8 AM. That gives us a two-hour window before service. Is that realistic given our current kitchen flow?

Two hours is tight but doable if we're organized. The beef is already braised overnight, so that's just reheating and plating prep. The tart dough is made ahead, so we're just assembling and baking. The sea bass and chicken are the time-critical items. If we batch the chicken and have the sea bass portioned and ready, we can manage it. But we need to be disciplined about the prep order.

I agree. The schedule works if we stick to it. One thing I want to flag: the allergen sheet in A6 needs to be double-checked. I've reviewed it and I see we have gluten flagged for the tart and the curry spice blend. But I want to make sure we've caught all 14 major allergens. Can we do a full audit before we finalize?

I can help with that. I'll go through each ingredient on the recipes and cross-check against the allergen list. The tart has dairy and gluten. The curry has sesame in the spice blend. The sea bass is clean. The chicken has no major allergens. The beef is clean. The vegetable dishes—I need to check the dressing on the plate.

The dressing on the vegetable plate has mustard, so that's a flag. I'll update A6 with all of that. Once we have the full allergen audit, we can finalize the reference sheet. That needs to be visible at the pass during service.

Good. So the prep schedule in A4 is locked pending the allergen audit. Once that's done, we have our daily workflow. The food safety checklist in A4 covers critical control points: storage temps, cooling procedures, reheating, and cross-contamination prevention. Does that cover everything we need?
The checklist looks comprehensive. One addition: we should note the specific reheating temps for the beef braise and the tart. Both need to hit 75°C minimum. I'll add that detail to A4.
Good catch. I'll also make sure the checklist includes a sign-off line so whoever does the prep can initial it. That creates accountability and a record if we ever need it.

I'll finalize A6 with the allergen audit by tomorrow morning. Once that's done, we can print both A4 and A6 and post them in the prep area. The schedule is ready to go. Should we do a walk-through with the team before we start using it?

Yes. Once A4 and A6 are finalized, we'll do a 30-minute walk-through with the full team. That way everyone knows the flow, the safety checks, and the allergen flags. That's locked in as D5 and D6. Let's aim for that walk-through by end of week.

threads.thread_goal: Run tasting, refine recipes, and lock plating and service guidelines.

messages.text: We ran the first internal tasting yesterday. All seven dishes were prepared and timed. I've captured the feedback in A7 Tasting Notes. Overall, the dishes tasted good, but we have some timing and plating adjustments to make. I've also drafted A5 Plating Guide with standard presentations for each dish. Let's review the notes and decide on adjustments.

I was at the tasting. The chicken was solid—good seasoning, consistent cook. The beef braise was tender but the sauce was a bit thin. We might need to reduce it longer or add a touch of cornstarch to thicken. The sea bass was excellent. Timing on all three proteins was about 12 minutes from start to plate, which is within our window.

The vegetable dishes came out well. The tart was crispy and the filling was balanced. The roasted vegetable plate was colorful and the dressing worked. The chickpea curry—the spice level was good but the consistency was a bit loose. I think we need to reduce the liquid slightly or add a bit more chickpeas to thicken it up.

Agreed on the curry. The flavor is there but the texture needs adjustment. I'd reduce the liquid by about 10% and see how that plays. For the beef sauce, I'd go with a light cornstarch slurry rather than reducing further—keeps the flavor intact. Both are minor tweaks.

On plating, the tart looked good as drafted. The vegetable plate could use a bit more height and structure—maybe stack the vegetables instead of laying them flat. The curry needs a garnish—cilantro or a drizzle of yogurt would lift it. The proteins all plated cleanly.

Good feedback. So the adjustments are: beef sauce gets a light cornstarch slurry, curry liquid reduced by 10%, vegetable plate gets stacked presentation, curry gets cilantro garnish. I'll update A2 with these recipe tweaks and A5 with the plating notes. Should we do a second tasting to confirm the changes work?

Yes, a second tasting makes sense. The changes are minor but we want to make sure the sauce consistency and curry texture are right before we lock it in. I can run that tasting tomorrow afternoon if you want to prep the adjusted recipes.
I'll prep the vegetable dishes with the new plating approach. The stacked presentation should work well. I'll have those ready by 2 PM tomorrow.
I'll handle the curry adjustment—reduce the liquid and test the consistency. Should be straightforward. The beef sauce adjustment is also simple. I'll have both ready for the tasting.

Perfect. I'll prep the chicken and sea bass with the plating notes from A5. We'll do a full run tomorrow at 2 PM. Once we confirm the adjustments, I'll finalize A2 and A5 and we'll be ready for the prep schedule walk-through.

Sounds good. After the second tasting, we'll have everything locked. The recipes will be finalized, the plating will be confirmed, and we can move into the final prep schedule walk-through. That puts us on track for launch next week.
Confirmed. Second tasting tomorrow at 2 PM. After that, we finalize everything and do the team walk-through. We're on schedule.

threads.thread_goal: Plan launch week operations and agree on tracking of sales and waste.

messages.text: We're ready for launch. I've drafted the launch week service plan and created A8 Sales and Waste Log template. The plan accounts for expected volumes and includes backup options for key items. We need to confirm the launch date and agree on how we'll track sales and waste during the first week.

Looking at the launch plan, I see we're starting with the full menu on day one. That's ambitious. Given that this is new, I'd suggest a phased approach: launch with four core dishes on day one, add the remaining three by day three. That gives us time to work out any kinks without overwhelming the team.

That's a smart approach. We can launch with the chicken, beef, sea bass, and curry—that covers all protein types and the vegan option. The vegetable dishes can come online by day three once we've settled the rhythm. The backup cod stays in reserve.

That works for prep too. We can focus on getting the four core dishes dialed in before adding the vegetable complexity. What's the launch date? I want to make sure we have enough time to do a final prep run.
I was thinking Monday of next week. That gives us the rest of this week to finalize everything and do a full dress rehearsal on Friday. Does Monday work for everyone?
Monday works. That's five days away. Plenty of time to prep and get comfortable with the new dishes. I'm ready.

Monday is good. Now, on the tracking in A8—I want to make sure we're capturing the right data. We need portions sold per dish, waste per dish, and any service issues. How are we recording this? Daily log at end of shift?

Yes, end of shift. The log is simple: dish name, portions sold, portions wasted, and notes on any issues. We'll do this daily for the first week, then weekly after that. The data helps us see what's working and what needs adjustment. I'll brief the team on how to fill it out.

That's straightforward. End-of-shift log, daily for week one. I can make sure the team knows how to record it. The template in A8 is clear. One thing: should we also note any customer feedback or special requests? That might be useful for tweaking.
Good idea. I'll add a 'notes' column to A8 for feedback. That way we capture everything in one place. Makes it easier to review at the end of the week.

Perfect. So we're locked on: launch Monday with four core dishes, add the vegetable options by day three, track sales and waste daily in A8 with a notes column for feedback. That's D9 and D10 confirmed. I'll finalize the launch plan and brief the team on Friday.
Sounds good. We're ready. The menu is locked, the recipes are finalized, the prep schedule is set, and we have a clear launch plan. Let's make this work.
